notes:
Account snapshot: trading analytics firm. High throughput real-time reranking + chat for trader desk assistants. Heavy sensitivity to tail latency during market open/close. Security: must run in VPC or on-prem with KMS/HSM; retention policy + audit logs mandatory.

Key technical asks (customer language captured):
- Sustained baseline throughput: ~15,000 tokens/sec across the cluster (avg request 120-200 tokens).
- Concurrency cap target: support 200-300 concurrent sessions with p95 latency goals.
- Burst policy: ability to burst to 45k tokens/sec for 60-90s windows during market events; bursts must not degrade baseline SLA.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 80ms for short prompts (<64 tokens), p95 < 250ms for typical prompts (<=256 tokens), for long form synthesis p95 < 800ms.
- Deterministic measurement windows and clear instrumentation: customer insists on token-counted measurement (server-side) and shared dashboards for verification.

What we've proposed (summary):
- Dedicated pool of 16x A10s (or equivalent) with reserved baseline capacity mapped to 12k tokens/sec + policy for pre-warmed burst pool to 40-45k tokens/sec.
- Concurrency shaping: request-level concurrency cap + queuing policy; recommended soft-queue with prioritized customer tokens for critical routes.
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to smaller/cheaper model for non-critical background jobs; explicit model-variant fallback defined in SLA.
- SLA language: credit model proposed based on hourly under-provisioning and % of measurement windows below agreed tokens/sec.

Negotiation pain points / customer pushback:
- They want guaranteed sustained 15k tokens/sec (not comfortable with 'best-effort' bursts).
- Concern about burst windows triggering queueing for other customers on same physical capacity; want isolation guarantees during market events.
- Legal wants crisp definitions: measurement interval, tokens counting, what constitutes 'force majeure' for burst spikes.
- Pricing delta for hard guarantees is large; procurement pushing to cap penalty exposure.

- Two-week performance POC in Redwood Dedicated demo cluster (week of 2026-03-10). SE to deploy their workload harness (JMeter + custom token profiler). Ticket QFR-POC-12 opened.
- Test scenarios: steady-state 15k tokens/sec for 2 hours, 45k tokens/sec 90s bursts x 5, failure-injection to validate fallback.
- Deliverables: token-level latency/time-series, p50/p95/p99, queue-depth metrics, CSV of raw requests, runbook for scaling.
